correctness.rationale: For every t>0, the H-principal tree branch Schur complement g is positive with g^{-1}>=h/3+t/h; this gives 0<P_bb<1 and strict adjacent entries. If any beta=h/6-t/h is positive, deletion of that edge and a distinct neighbor gives P_vw=-beta*g_v*P_uw<0. If every beta<=0, H is SPD Stieltjes and H^{-1}M>=0. t=0 gives I, and the two-vertex case has no distance-two obstruction. Exact rational testing executes 411 independently assembled cases, but infinity is covered by proof.

value.rationale: A complete all-tree, grading-independent necessity/sufficiency classification solves the natural nonnegativity design question for Kirchhoff heat-network time stepping. Every edge violating the longest-element rule yields an explicit two-hop negative witness, a substantive local diagnostic absent from general one-way Stieltjes tests; branching is unrestricted and the two-vertex boundary is sharp. No general PDE convergence or higher-order method claim is made.
